description: We are a team of three passionate technology enthusiasts interested in software development, AI, data science, and innovative problem-solving. Our team has experience participating in development hackathons, building software projects, and exploring emerging technologies. We aim to develop a reliable and interactive solution for harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data, making satellite-based fire monitoring more accessible and meaningful.
summary:
PROJECT MARSBOUND is a browser-native 3D human planetary survival simulator and interactive mission operations guide engineered for Gale Crater, Mars. Developed for future astronauts and STEM students, the platform replaces static technical documentation with a gamified, physics-accurate operational mission.

The experience begins at Kennedy Space Center Launch Pad 39B with an astronaut gantry walkout and rocket ascent, transitioning directly into atmospheric entry and Gale Crater exploration. Players navigate real-world Martian topography calibrated against NASA MOLA elevation models, managing life support via the NASA Pandolf bioenergetics model. Survival depends on mastering six progressive In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) modules: MOXIE carbon-dioxide oxygen cracking, SHARAD subsurface glacial ice harvesting, regolith radiation shielding, inflatable habitat pressurization, 6-wheel rocker-bogie rover locomotion, and autonomous colony microgrids. 

Crucially, the platform features a zero-virtual-joystick physical phone sensor link: students scan a QR code to sync their smartphone’s accelerometer and gyroscope, allowing physical real-world footsteps to propel their astronaut across the Martian surface. It runs at 60 FPS in any standard browser without gaming hardware.
details:
1. WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

PROJECT MARSBOUND places students in the pilot seat of a human expedition to Gale Crater (4.589°S, 137.441°E). The application is powered by Three.js and React Three Fiber WebGL rendering, with physics governed by a custom 60 Hz planetary gravity engine (0.38G). Locomotion uses swept-segment continuous collision resolution against 68 physical basalt boulders, hab domes, and rovers to eliminate tunneling. Players can board two rovers (an open exploration rover and an enclosed 6x6 pressurized expedition rover) and launch or retro-land a heavy-lift rocket with thrust deceleration.

2. WHAT BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT DOES IT HAVE?

Most space educational tools rely on static diagrams or pre-rendered videos. MARSBOUND makes planetary science tactile and kinesthetic. By feeling metabolic heart-rate changes under low gravity, calculating oxygen production rates (10.0 g/hr at 800°C) with MOXIE, and analyzing CRISM hyperspectral mineral signatures (Nontronite, Hematite, Kieserite, Boxwork), students gain an intuitive, empirical understanding of aerospace engineering challenges.

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & HARDWARE USED:

- Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Next.js architecture

- 3D Engine & Shaders: Three.js, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, GLSL atmospheric Rayleigh/Mie scattering sky shaders

- 3D Modeling & Animation: Blender 5.3 (quad topology modeling, bone armature skeletal rigging, and baked 4K PBR textures)

- Physics & Animation: Custom multi-pass sliding collision solver, Anime.js tweening

- Mobile Sensor Relay: HTML5 DeviceOrientation & DeviceMotion APIs with real-time SSE streaming for zero-joystick pedometer walking

- Deployment: Vercel Global Edge Network with immutable CDN asset caching for 3D GLTF models

4. HOW IS IT CREATIVE & WHAT FACTORS WERE CONSIDERED?

- Zero-Virtual-Joystick Locomotion: Eliminates clunky on-screen touch joysticks by using the phone's physical accelerometer to detect human footsteps, syncing real-world walking to the astronaut’s stride.

- Real NASA Planetary Data: All terrain elevations, atmospheric pressures (780 Pa), diurnal temperatures (-74°C to -28°C), and mineral absorption bands are pulled directly from Curiosity, Perseverance, and MRO datasets.

- Industrial Aerospace HUD: Built using strict contrast guidelines, IBM Plex typography, and tabular numeric alignment to avoid digit jitter, creating an authentic mission control environment.
